events.title: Brent Crosses $100 After Houthi Tanker Attacks Off Saudi Arabia; Fed September Hike Odds Surge to 82%; Dow Falls 600+ Points
events.detail: Brent crude jumped about 7% to close at $100.69/barrel on July 23 — its first close above $100 since late May — after Iran-backed Houthi militants said they struck two Saudi Arabian tankers in the Red Sea, opening a new front alongside the ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruptions and threatening the detour route Saudi Arabia had been using to keep barrels flowing. The attacks came hours after Trump warned the US would strike an Iranian bridge or power plant for every future Hormuz tanker attack, and Iran threatened retaliation against US-linked regional infrastructure. US gasoline averaged $4/gallon. The renewed geopolitical energy shock, combined with weekly jobless claims plunging to 187,000 (vs. 212,000 expected, the lowest since 1969), pushed fed funds futures to price roughly an 82% chance of a Fed hike at the September FOMC meeting — up more than 29 points from a week earlier — and a 38% chance of a hike at the following week's July 28-29 meeting (up from 12%). The 10-year Treasury yield rose to its highest level since January 2025. Equity markets sold off sharply: the Dow fell more than 600 points and the Nasdaq lost nearly 3%.

events.title: Section 122 Tariff Cliff 8 Days Out — No Congressional Action Reported; Section 301 Fallback Timing Still in Doubt
events.detail: With the Section 122 tariff authority set to expire July 24 — 8 days away — no Congressional action has been reported and none is expected; an extension would require 60 Senate votes, and there is no indication Congress plans to act. The administration's intended fallback, Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies over forced-labor practices, remained in the proposal/hearing stage as of July 7, with a 30-day pre-effect notice requirement that puts its readiness by July 24 in serious doubt — raising the prospect of a tariff-revenue coverage gap at the cliff date. Separately, the next FOMC meeting is scheduled for July 28-29 — a non-SEP meeting with no new dot plot — where consensus expects another hold at 3.50-3.75%. China's Politburo meeting, expected in late July, is being watched for fresh stimulus signals after the Q2 GDP miss.

events.title: Day 692 — US Reopens Border to Mexican Cattle Exports at Agua Prieta, Sonora After 14-Month Screwworm Ban
events.detail: On August 24, 2026 (Day 692, Monday), the United States reopened the Agua Prieta (Sonora)–Douglas (Arizona) crossing to Mexican cattle exports, ending a suspension imposed after the first New World screwworm (gusano barrenador) case was detected in a Chiapas bovine in November 2024; the ban had blocked roughly 1.7 million head of cattle worth an estimated $2.2 billion. President Sheinbaum said she received a letter from U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins notifying her of the decision. The reopening follows a joint SADER–SENASICA–USDA sanitary action plan and enhanced traceability across a 200-km radius in Sonora and Chihuahua; an initial shipment of roughly 750 head crossed on the first day, with a target of 1,700–2,000 head per day at full capacity. Additional crossings — San Jerónimo-Santa Teresa and Puerto Palomas-Columbus, both linking Chihuahua to New Mexico — are slated to follow in a staggered rollout.

events.title: Day 692 — Sheinbaum Calls PRI's Alito Moreno "Entreguista, Traidor" Over US Tour, Flags $120K Consultancy Contract to INE
events.detail: On August 24, 2026 (Day 692, Monday), President Sheinbaum escalated her criticism of PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno Cárdenas, calling him "entreguista, traidor" over his repeated trips to Washington to lobby U.S. officials against her government. She said it was up to the INE to determine whether Moreno's reported $120,000-a-month contract with Washington firm Concord Hill Strategies — covering trip logistics and image/wardrobe coaching for his meetings with Trump administration and Congressional officials — violated Mexican political-party financing rules, adding that his "funciones están en EEUU y no en México." The comments follow Interior Undersecretary Ariadna Montiel's earlier accusation that Moreno's US visits sought "protección" from domestic corruption investigations. Separately, Sheinbaum said she was not consulted on Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya's brief Aug 21 return to office — "me enteré por la publicación" — and deferred to the state Congress on the succession.

events.title: Day 691 — Sinaloa Congress Unanimously Approves Rocha Moya's Indefinite Leave
events.detail: On August 23, 2026 (Day 691, Sunday), the Sinaloa state Congress met in an extraordinary session and voted unanimously (all nine deputies present) to approve Rubén Rocha Moya's indefinite leave from the governorship, two days after he briefly returned to the post over a U.S. DOJ indictment tying him to the Sinaloa Cartel's "Los Chapitos" faction. Deputies deferred the question of who becomes interim governor to a Monday, August 24 session at 11:00 a.m., with General Secretary of Government Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde — who had already served as interim governor once, from May to August — administering the state in the meantime and seen as a likely pick to resume the role.

events.title: Day 690 — Rocha Moya Requests Indefinite Leave Again After Sheinbaum, Morena Distance Themselves
events.detail: On August 22, 2026 (Day 690, Saturday) at 6:40 p.m., Rubén Rocha Moya requested leave from the Sinaloa governorship for a second time — an indefinite leave submitted by letter to the state Congress — just one day after unilaterally reincorporating himself into the post over the April 29 U.S. DOJ indictment tying him to the Sinaloa Cartel's "Los Chapitos" faction. President Sheinbaum publicly distanced herself from his return, saying "Sinaloa, la nación y el movimiento de transformación están por encima de todo" and that "ningún interés personal" should be placed above "los intereses del pueblo y de la Nación," warning against "ambición desnuda del poder por el poder"; Morena and the Interior Secretariat also publicly broke with him. Former DEA director Derek Maltz called for Rocha's arrest and deportation. The Sinaloa Congress suspended its session to select an interim governor, postponing the decision.

events.title: Day 690 — Sheinbaum Inaugurates Archivo General Agrario in Mexico City
events.detail: On August 22, 2026 (Day 690, Saturday), President Sheinbaum inaugurated the Centro Nacional de Atención Agraria and Archivo General Agrario in Mexico City — a facility housing the Registro Agrario Nacional, the Procuraduría Agraria, and the country's historical agrarian records. Agrarian Secretary Edna Elena Vega Rangel called it "the second in importance after the Archivo General de la Nación," with over 45,000 linear meters of documents, including more than 100,000 maps and land-tenure records dating to 1917 and colonial-era materials, plus the decrees of all Fourth Transformation land-restitution grants (60,000+ hectares to date). Construction began in 2022 under President López Obrador on land donated by Sheinbaum during her tenure as Mexico City mayor.

events.title: Day 689 — Sheinbaum Misses Mañanera With Flu, Reappears Masked for Virtual IMSS Meeting
events.detail: On August 21, 2026 (Day 689, Friday), President Sheinbaum woke up with a severe flu, cough and fever and — for the first time in her presidency — did not lead the daily morning press conference; doctors recommended rest, though her office said the condition was not serious and ruled out COVID-19. Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez led the conference in her place alongside INAH director Joel Omar Vázquez Herrera, who presented a discovery of 179 pre-Hispanic pieces and 13 offerings in the Cueva Mundo Zoque cave in Cintalapa, Chiapas. Sheinbaum kept working remotely from the National Palace, appearing on camera wearing a face mask for a virtual meeting with IMSS director Zoé Robledo reviewing progress on the Universal Health Service (Servicios de Salud) rollout. Her team said she expected to resume in-person activities the next day, including a planned Saturday inauguration of the Archivo General Agrario de la Nación in Mexico City.

events.title: Day 689 — Rocha Moya Returns as Sinaloa Governor, Defying US DOJ Indictment
events.detail: On August 21, 2026 (Day 689, Friday) at 12:07 p.m., Rubén Rocha Moya announced his reincorporation as constitutional governor of Sinaloa, ending a 112-day leave he had requested May 1-2 after an April 29 U.S. District Court (Southern District of New York) indictment charged him and nine other current and former Sinaloa officials with conspiracy to import narcotics, weapons possession, and institutional protection of the Sinaloa Cartel's "Los Chapitos" faction. Rocha rejected the charges and returned without first consulting the federal government or Morena party leadership; interim governor Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde, who had held the post since May 2, stepped aside and returned to the Secretaría General de Gobierno as Rocha took protest. The move came a day after the U.S. reiterated that "the Sinaloa Cartel could not operate without the help of corrupt officials."

events.title: Day 688 — Sheinbaum Unveils "Olinia de Carga" Electric Cargo Vehicle
events.detail: On August 20, 2026 (Day 688, Thursday), President Sheinbaum unveiled "Olinia de Carga" in the Palacio Nacional courtyard — the second Olinia electric vehicle after the passenger model presented June 7, 2026. The cargo version carries up to 650 kg (up to 12 stackable huacal crates), was engineered by roughly 70 specialists based in Puebla through Mexico's public universities, and is projected to sell for about 150,000 pesos by late 2027. Production will use mixed public-private investment; a public bidding process opens in late September 2026 with formal offers due in November, targeting initial output of 10,000 units per year scaling toward 50,000 per year.

events.title: Day 688 — Michoacán CJNG Operation Toll Rises to 12 Detained; Tío Lako Still at Large
events.detail: On August 20, 2026 (Day 688, Thursday), authorities raised the toll from the prior day's federal operation against Tío Lako's CJNG cell in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo, Michoacán to 12 people detained — his daughter, partner and 10 others — while Tío Lako (Heraclio Guerrero Martínez) himself remained at large. SEDENA, the National Guard, SSPC and the Navy jointly carried out the raids, seizing 64 vehicles (one armored), a .50-caliber machine gun, four 5.56mm mini machine guns, nine long rifles, a handgun, grenade-launcher attachments, eight improvised explosive devices, a drone and ammunition. Officials again linked the crackdown to Tío Lako's alleged orders to attack National Guard troops after the February 22, 2026 SEDENA operation in Tapalpa, Jalisco that killed CJNG leader Rubén "El Mencho" Oseguera Cervantes and Tío Lako's son, Rubén "El R1" Guerrero Valadez.

events.title: Day 687 — Federal Operation Against CJNG's "Tío Lako" Cell Sparks Michoacán Narco-Blockades
events.detail: On August 19, 2026 (Day 687, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum confirmed at her mañanera an active federal operation to detain "one or several priority objectives" in Michoacán, with the Security Cabinet to brief details later that day. Army-led raids in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo targeted a CJNG cell run by regional plaza boss Heraclio Guerrero Martínez, alias "Tío Lako"; he evaded capture, but 9 people were detained, including his daughter Marisol "N" and partner Lourdes "N." The operation triggered more than 20 narco-blockades and vehicle burnings on highways across Zamora, La Piedad, Ecuandureo, Zacapu, Chilchota and Tangancícuaro, and an armed clash left a preliminary 5 civilians dead. Officials tied the crackdown to Tío Lako's alleged orders to attack National Guard troops after the February 22, 2026 SEDENA operation in Tapalpa, Jalisco that killed CJNG leader Rubén "El Mencho" Oseguera Cervantes and Tío Lako's own son, Rubén "El R1" Guerrero Valadez.

events.title: Day 687 — Sheinbaum Calls Detained Argentine Strategist Cerimedo a "Feminicida," Accuses La Derecha Diario of Running Bot Network
events.detail: On August 19, 2026 (Day 687, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum reacted to the August 18 detention in Bolivia of Argentine right-wing strategist Fernando Cerimedo — a former adviser to Javier Milei and founder of La Derecha Diario — after his ex-wife Nadia Beller accused him of hiring hitmen to attempt to kill her while she was pregnant; Bolivian prosecutors sought 180 days of preventive detention. Sheinbaum said Cerimedo was "a feminicida, in short words, who attacked his wife multiple times," and separately accused La Derecha Diario of amplifying attacks on her government through a bot network, describing it as part of a coordinated international right-wing media operation.

events.title: Day 687 — Sheinbaum Unveils 147B-Peso PODECOBI Industrial Pole in Zapotlán, Hidalgo
events.detail: On August 19, 2026 (Day 687, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum and Hidalgo Governor Julio Menchaca presented the PODECOBI (Polo de Desarrollo Económico para el Bienestar) industrial pole in Zapotlán: 130 projects worth 147 billion pesos across 910 hectares, projected to create 191,000 jobs in manufacturing, logistics, pharmaceuticals and medical devices. Lead investors include DEWA Capital (10.1 billion pesos for an industrial complex, ~5,100 jobs in its initial phase) and Cooperativa Cruz Azul (6.5 billion pesos to expand cement production and modernize hospital infrastructure in nearby Tula, ~14,200 jobs).

events.title: Day 686 — Gasoline Shortage in CDMX, Chiapas, Nuevo León Resolved; 1 Million Women Register for Pensión Bienestar
events.detail: On August 18, 2026 (Day 686, Tuesday), President Sheinbaum said a gasoline supply shortage affecting Mexico City, Chiapas, and Nuevo León had been resolved, calling it 'cosa de unos días.' Welfare Secretary Ariadna Montiel reported that more than 1 million women had registered for the Pensión Mujeres Bienestar program since applications opened August 1 for women aged 60 and above. Profeco director Iván Escalante presented the latest '¿Quién es Quién?' price-comparison balance tracking gasoline, groceries, and remittance-service pricing nationwide. Sheinbaum also addressed the ongoing visa revocation of Andy López Beltrán, denying his implication in the fuel-theft ('huachicol fiscal') probe and calling U.S. scrutiny of him politically motivated, and said she would meet Morena's congressional coordinators Adán Augusto López and Ricardo Monreal that afternoon on legislative priorities.

events.title: Day 682 — Peso Strengthens to 16.98/USD as Sheinbaum Confirms Tamaulipas Hospital Tour
events.detail: On August 14, 2026 (Day 682, Friday), Sheinbaum noted the peso trading at 16.98 per US dollar and said she expects H2 2026 growth to strengthen as previously delayed public works — held up mainly by bureaucratic bottlenecks — begin construction: 'Each month is going to be better.' She also confirmed a weekend work tour to Tamaulipas with Governor Américo Villarreal to inaugurate two new hospitals (ISSSTE and IMSS-Bienestar), review hydraulic works, and meet with 'Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro' participants.

events.title: Day 681 — AMLO's Son Andy López Beltrán Says US Revoked His Visa, Adding Pressure on Sheinbaum
events.detail: On August 13, 2026 (Day 681, Thursday), Andrés Manuel 'Andy' López Beltrán — son of former president AMLO — announced via a letter posted to Instagram and addressed to Donald Trump that the U.S. State Department, under Secretary Marco Rubio and Deputy Secretary Christopher Landau, had revoked his U.S. visa. López Beltrán called the move 'political, more propagandistic than anything, in a Hitlerian style' and denied any wrongdoing. The episode increased scrutiny on the Sheinbaum government amid separate PAN questions linking López Beltrán to an FGR fuel-theft ('huachicol fiscal') investigation.

events.title: Day 680 — Sheinbaum Meets Goldman Sachs President Waldron to Discuss Plan México Investment
events.detail: On August 12, 2026 (Day 680, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum met at the National Palace with Goldman Sachs President and COO John E. Waldron, alongside Finance Secretary Edgar Amador Zamora, to discuss Mexico's 'favorable perception' among international investors and opportunities under Plan México, which targets 1.5 million new jobs and investment above 25% of GDP as Mexico aims to move from the world's 15th- to a top-10 economy. No specific investment agreements or new projects were disclosed following the meeting.

events.title: Day 676 — US Partially Resumes Avocado Inspections After Mexico Deploys 1,557 Troops to Michoacán
events.detail: On August 8, 2026 (Day 676, Saturday), the U.S. Embassy began a partial resumption of avocado export inspections in Michoacán, three days after the August 5 suspension, covering the municipalities of Tancítaro, Tacámbaro, Uruapan, and the Morelia–Pátzcuaro corridor. The restart followed a security agreement under which the Mexican government deployed 1,557 Army and National Guard personnel to the avocado belt on August 6 and established a permanent coordination table to monitor conditions protecting U.S. inspectors. The resumption remained partial and contingent on continued security improvements, with full normalization pending across the roughly 60 export packing plants in the state.

events.title: Trump Says US Will Raise Canada Auto, Parts, and Steel Tariffs to 50% on Jan. 1, 2027
events.detail: President Trump announced on Truth Social on Monday, August 24, 2026 that tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel would rise to 50% effective January 1, 2027, doubling the current 25% rate applied to non-US content, and declaring 'Canada will be treated like a State no longer.' The threat follows the collapse of US-Canada trade talks on August 21 and the 50% tariffs already in effect on roughly $20 billion of other Canadian goods; Trump accused Canada of 'ripping off the United States of America for years.' Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has vowed to retaliate 'dollar for dollar,' with Canada's countermeasures targeting US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper, and electronics starting September 8.

events.title: Trump Says US Will Raise Canada Auto, Parts, and Steel Tariffs to 50% on Jan. 1, 2027
events.detail: President Trump announced on Truth Social on Monday, August 24, 2026 that tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel would rise to 50% effective January 1, 2027, doubling the current 25% rate applied to non-US content, and declaring 'Canada will be treated like a State no longer.' The threat follows the collapse of US-Canada trade talks on August 21 and the 50% tariffs already in effect on roughly $20 billion of other Canadian goods; Trump accused Canada of 'ripping off the United States of America for years.' Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has vowed to retaliate 'dollar for dollar,' with Canada's countermeasures targeting US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper, and electronics starting September 8.

events.title: US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse, 50% Tariffs on $20B of Canadian Goods Take Effect
events.detail: Trade negotiations between the US and Canada fell apart late Friday night, August 21, 2026, just before a midnight deadline — a dramatic reversal from Trump's August 18 announcement that the two sides 'have a DEAL!' Prime Minister Mark Carney said the US 'asked too much, and offered too little' with last-minute changes to the terms, including efforts to restrict Canada's ability to strike other trade deals and to weaken French-language and cultural protections tied to Canada's Online Streaming Act; Washington had also refused to extend tariff relief to medium and heavy trucks. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Canada 'declined to finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week,' while Trump posted that Canada 'wants the benefits of being a State, without being one.' With talks suspended, 50% Section 338 tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian dairy, alcohol, furniture, and other goods took effect; Carney vowed 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper, and electronics starting September 8.

events.title: Trump Pauses 50% Canada Tariffs for 3 Days as Trade Deal Nears Completion
events.detail: President Trump announced late Tuesday, August 18, 2026 that he was pausing the 50% Section 338 tariffs on Canadian imports — set to take effect the next morning, August 19 — for a three-day period, saying on Truth Social that the US and Canada 'have a deal!' subject to finalizing the paperwork. The tariffs, announced July 20 and covering roughly $16-20 billion of Canadian dairy, agriculture, furniture, alcohol, and vehicle imports, had been set to kick in hours after Trump's post. Prime Minister Mark Carney's government had been racing to close a deal with Washington before the deadline; the pause buys both sides additional time to finalize terms.

events.title: US National Debt Surpasses $40 Trillion, Months Ahead of Forecasts
events.detail: The US Treasury Department's daily statement showed total public debt outstanding crossing $40.05 trillion on August 18-19, 2026 — a record that arrived months earlier than forecasters had expected, driven partly by lost tariff revenue after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's IEEPA tariffs in February. The debt has more than doubled since 2017 and reached the milestone just five months after crossing $39 trillion in March 2026; the debt-to-GDP ratio stands near a record 123%. The Bipartisan Policy Center estimates the US will hit the $41.1 trillion debt ceiling sometime between late winter and mid-summer 2027, forcing Congress to again vote on raising or suspending the limit.

events.title: Treasury Proposes GENIUS Act Rules Restricting Who Can Issue Stablecoins
events.detail: The US Treasury Department published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking on August 18, 2026 in the Federal Register implementing Section 3 of the GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law Trump signed in 2025, seeking public comment on which entities may lawfully issue payment stablecoins in the United States. Under the proposal, only federally or state-licensed issuers could offer stablecoins in the US starting July 18, 2028, with violations carrying fines up to $1 million and up to five years in prison. The GENIUS Act is due to take full effect January 18, 2027, though the law's original one-year deadline for finalizing implementing rules already passed in July without full compliance. Comments on the proposed rule are due by October 19, 2026.

events.title: US Imposes New 10% Section 301 Tariff on Mexico Over Forced-Labor Import Enforcement Gaps
events.detail: The Office of the US Trade Representative announced the results of a Section 301 forced-labor investigation covering 60 economies, imposing new ad valorem tariffs effective July 24–25, 2026. Mexico was placed in the more favorable 10% tier (rather than the 12.5% tier applied to countries with no forced-labor import prohibition at all) because USTR determined it has import bans on the books but has failed to effectively enforce them against goods transiting its supply chains. Crucially, Mexican goods that qualify for duty-free treatment under USMCA rules of origin remain exempt from the new tariff, so the measure primarily affects the roughly 11-16% of Mexico-US trade that does not claim USMCA preference. The action landed in the middle of the ongoing USMCA joint-review negotiations and added a new friction point alongside earlier tariff threats on autos, steel, aluminum, and copper.

events.title: Trump Threatens 30% Reciprocal Tariff on Mexico Starting August 1
events.detail: President Trump announced that reciprocal tariffs on Mexican goods would rise to 30% effective August 1, 2026, escalating pressure during the ongoing USMCA joint review process. The threat came roughly two weeks after the US declined to renew USMCA on its current 16-year terms at the July 1 joint review, and as bilateral negotiating rounds on automotive rules of origin, steel, and aluminum continued. As of mid-July, USMCA-qualifying goods (an estimated 89% of Mexico-US trade) continued to enter under the existing 0% preferential rate, with the 30% threat aimed at non-qualifying goods and intended as leverage ahead of the next negotiating round scheduled for the week of July 20.

events.title: Banxico Holds Benchmark Rate at 6.5% in Unanimous Vote, Signals End of Easing Cycle
events.detail: The Bank of Mexico's governing board unanimously voted to hold its benchmark interest rate at 6.5% at its June 25, 2026 meeting, confirming the two-year easing cycle that began in March 2024 has concluded. Headline inflation continued to ease, falling from 4.45% in April to 3.55% by mid-June, within Banxico's target tolerance range. Policymakers signaled they will likely keep the rate at this level going forward, citing upside risks from trade disruptions tied to the ongoing USMCA review, geopolitical tensions, persistent core inflation, and possible peso depreciation.

events.title: Banxico Cuts Benchmark Rate to 6.5% in Split Vote, Signals End of Two-Year Easing Cycle
events.detail: Mexico's central bank (Banco de México / Banxico) voted 3-2 to cut its benchmark overnight interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.5% — the lowest level since May 2022 — following April inflation data showing a first deceleration since December 2025. The governing board simultaneously signaled this cut marked the end of a two-year-plus easing cycle that had lowered rates from the August 2023 peak of 11.25%. Board members in the minority voted to hold rates, citing continued uncertainty over US tariff impacts on inflation and peso stability. The peso traded at approximately 17.31 per dollar in early May, representing significant strengthening from the 2025 average of approximately 19.20. The rate decision comes against a complex macroeconomic backdrop: while inflation is moderating and the peso has strengthened, Mexico's economy contracted in Q1 2026 (largest decline in over a year) with investment falling 6.6% in 2025. The Banxico decision was interpreted as a signal that monetary policy has done its work and that structural reforms — fiscal stimulus, investment promotion through Plan México Acciones — must now carry the weight of economic revival. The 6.5% rate still provides meaningful real interest rates above the approximately 4% headline inflation reading, preserving Mexico's financial stability credentials.

events.title: Mexico's Labor Poverty Rate Hits Historic Low at 32.3% in Q4 2025, Despite GDP Contraction Warnings
events.detail: Mexico's Labor Ministry (STPS) and CONEVAL released Q4 2025 labor poverty data on May 6, 2026, confirming a historic milestone: the share of Mexicans in households unable to cover basic food needs with wage income fell to 32.3% — the lowest on record since the measure was introduced. Labor Minister Marath Bolaños highlighted the figure as evidence that the minimum wage increases (cumulative 283% since 2018 under AMLO and Sheinbaum) have translated into genuine material gains for low-income workers. Mexico raised the minimum wage again in January 2026 to MX$278.80/day (approximately $16.10/day), the highest nominal level since the modern wage was established. However, the milestone came amid contradictory signals: the Q1 2026 GDP contraction of 0.8% — confirmed by INEGI on April 30 — created downside risk for formal employment in the near term. Bloomberg's May 6 analysis argued that 'Mexico will lose more from a bad USMCA rewrite than from no deal,' noting that the agreement generates approximately $839 billion in annual bilateral trade and sustains millions of formal jobs in manufacturing, agriculture, and services. The labor poverty reduction is credited to formal job creation driven by nearshoring investment — FDI into Mexico's manufacturing sector hit $36.9 billion in 2024, the highest on record — and the sustained minimum wage policy. Critics noted that 32.3% labor poverty still means nearly one in three Mexicans cannot cover basic food needs through labor income alone.

events.title: Mexico's Sovereign Infrastructure Fund (MIP) Seeks to Deploy $12 Billion; World Cup Airspace Security Decree Published
events.detail: Mexico's sovereign infrastructure fund (Fondo Mexicano del Petróleo para la Estabilización y el Desarrollo, MIP) announced it is actively seeking to deploy USD $12 billion in new infrastructure investments — a major complement to the Plan México Acciones framework unveiled the previous day. The deployment targets strategic infrastructure including ports, rail corridors, industrial parks, and energy grid upgrades to support the nearshoring manufacturing boom. Separately, on May 5, Mexico's Secretariat of National Defense (SEDENA) published a formal decree establishing four Zones of Surveillance and Protection of Mexican Airspace (ZVP) for the FIFA World Cup period running from May 11 through July 20, 2026 — covering Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey. The decree operationalizes Mexico's counter-drone (CUAS) commitments and coordinates military airspace control with civilian aviation authorities. Mexico City's Benito Juárez Airport simultaneously completed three-day tactical exercises simulating hijacking, hostage-taking, and CBRN (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear) scenarios. The dual announcements — major investment mobilization and World Cup security finalization — reflected the Sheinbaum government's effort to project institutional capacity despite the Sinaloa governor crisis and US sovereignty disputes of the preceding week.

events.title: Sheinbaum Unveils Plan México Acciones: MX$5.6 Trillion Infrastructure Push to Revive Contracting Economy
events.detail: President Claudia Sheinbaum unveiled 'Plan México Acciones,' an expanded investment framework designed to reverse Mexico's economic contraction after Q1 2026 posted the country's largest GDP decline in over a year. The plan encompasses a MX$5.6 trillion (approximately USD $407 billion) public-private infrastructure investment pipeline for 2026–2030, immediate accelerated tax deductions of 41–91% on new fixed-asset investments, and a unified digital foreign trade platform to reduce bureaucratic friction for exporters. Mexico's sovereign infrastructure fund (MIP) separately announced plans to deploy USD $12 billion in new infrastructure projects. The plan directly responds to a 2025 investment contraction of 6.6% — driven by investor uncertainty over the judicial reform, USMCA tariff tensions, and security concerns. Sheinbaum framed the initiative as Mexico's response to the nearshoring opportunity, with dozens of Asian and US manufacturing companies seeking to relocate supply chains from China to Mexico. The plan attracted cautious interest from the private sector, though business associations noted that judicial certainty and rule-of-law improvements — not tax incentives alone — were the primary investment constraints. Bloomberg noted the initiative came as Mexico sought to project economic confidence ahead of the May 25 USMCA formal review round.

events.title: INEGI Flash Estimate: Mexico's Economy Contracted 0.8% in Q1 2026, All Sectors Declined
events.detail: Mexico's national statistics agency (INEGI) released its flash GDP estimate for Q1 2026 on April 30, showing the economy contracted 0.8% quarter-over-quarter — the worst sequential decline since Q4 2024 and a steeper fall than market consensus. All three major sectors declined: primary activities (agriculture, livestock, fishing) fell 1.4%; industrial activities (manufacturing, construction, mining) fell 1.1%; and tertiary activities (services, commerce, tourism) declined 0.6%. Year-over-year, the economy grew only 0.2% in seasonally adjusted terms, essentially stagnating. The contraction reflected: continued investment uncertainty stemming from the 2024 judicial reform's impact on rule-of-law perceptions; the 25% US tariff on non-USMCA qualifying goods weighing on export-oriented manufacturing; construction delays in major government infrastructure projects; and a deceleration in consumption spending. The data directly prompted Sheinbaum to announce Plan México Acciones four days later (May 4) — a MX$5.6 trillion public-private investment framework intended to reverse the contraction trend. Banxico responded with a 25bp rate cut to 6.5% (May 7). Mexico's full-year 2026 GDP growth forecast was revised down to approximately 1.3%, driven largely by the anticipated World Cup tourism boost in Q2–Q3.

events.title: Sheinbaum Signs Steel Industry Promotion Agreement: All Federal Projects Must Use Mexican Steel
events.detail: President Claudia Sheinbaum signed the 'Acuerdo para el Fomento de la Industria Siderúrgica Nacional' (Agreement for the Promotion of the National Steel Industry) on April 29, 2026, requiring all federal public works projects to use domestically produced steel and iron. The agreement covers 19 federal agencies and three industry chambers — the Cámara Nacional del Acero (Canacero), the Cámara Nacional de la Industria de la Construcción (CNIC), and the Cámara Mexicana de la Industria de la Construcción (CMIC). Anti-Corruption Minister Raquel Buenrostro was designated as the deal's enforcer. Canacero chief Sergio de la Maza called it a 'decisive step' for import substitution, protecting approximately 90,000 direct jobs and providing certainty for over $8 billion in ongoing investment. For 2026, the public sector committed to procuring 150,000 tonnes of reinforcing steel, 150,000 tonnes of structural steel, and over one million tonnes for railway construction. The measure was Sheinbaum's direct economic response after bilateral negotiations to lift US steel and aluminum tariffs failed to reach agreement ahead of the USMCA formal review. By redirecting the government's construction purchasing power — which consumes approximately 60% of Mexico's domestic steel — toward national producers, Mexico essentially launched an import-substitution strategy in the steel sector without a retaliatory tariff. The agreement was unveiled at Wednesday's mañanera alongside the MX$5.6 trillion Plan México Acciones framework announced May 4.
